sections.html:
The quickest path is a cash purchase: the buyer accepts the house untouched and a title company deals with the deed and any payoffs. A regular listing reaches more people yet brings showings, inspections and a lender's timetable.

Paris is the Lamar County seat in Northeast Texas, so the courthouse, the clerk and the appraisal district are all in town. Deed, tax certificate and ownership papers can all be sorted out within a few blocks, which helps if a deadline is closing in.

The housing stock is old by Texas standards. The town dates to 1844, rail arrived in 1876, and fires in 1877 and 1916 forced rebuilding. A tornado on April 2, 1982 destroyed more than 1,500 homes, and nearly $7 million went into downtown renovation afterward. Anyone buying an older house will ask how old the roof, wiring and foundation are, so hold on to repair receipts and insurance claims. Disclose any known damage plainly in the contract.

sections.h2: Who values and collects the tax
sections.html:
Property values for the whole county come from the Lamar Central Appraisal District, and separate taxing units choose the rates. Find the office at 521 Bonham Street or call (903) 785-7822. Employees there field questions on values and exemptions and will point you to the collecting office.

Put a protest in writing by May 31, or within 30 days of the notice being mailed if that falls later. The state calendar prints May 15 for most protests, so read the date at the bottom of your own notice. Hearings begin around June 1, and a letter arrives about 15 days before yours.

Protest and penalty timing
StepTiming
Written protest dueMay 31, or 30 days from mailing of notice if later
Hearings beginAround June 1
Hearing letterAbout 15 days before your hearing
Penalty waiver paymentWithin 21 days after you learn of the delinquency
Waiver request filedBefore day 181 after the delinquency date

Back taxes can be paid off before closing or from the sale proceeds. A penalty waiver is often available when you pay inside 21 days of finding out about the delinquency and send a written request before day 181.

A few collectors allow installment plans stretching to 36 months, and a residence homestead is eligible. The appraised value of a homestead is also limited to a 10 percent yearly rise, starting the year after the exemption is first granted.

  • If a unit brings in a private attorney, up to 20 percent more can be added.
  • Full payment at closing ends the penalties.
  • Have the collector quote a total good for your closing date.

Before a buyer closes, an heir has to show who owns the house, and what that takes varies with the estate. Probate of a will normally has to happen within four years of death, in the county where the owner lived.

  • Muniment of title. A court order paired with the will, recorded with the clerk where the property lies.
  • Small estate affidavit. Works for estates under the $75,000 cap, homestead left out, when there is no will and every heir agrees.
  • Affidavit of heirship. A sworn statement, which no law requires outsiders to accept.

Ownership papers go to the Lamar County clerk. Whichever route you take, the buyer will want to see the paper that lets you sign.

Pull the deed and latest tax statement first, then the lender's payoff contact and any lease. Expect the title company to request exactly these.

  • Photo ID from every person named on the deed.
  • Death certificate and court papers if an owner has died.
  • A signed lease and deposit record if tenants live there.
  • Receipts for roof, wiring or foundation work.

Put in writing who orders the title policy and who pays for it.

sections.h2: What buyers look at in Paris
sections.html:
The town is a regional medical and shopping center for Northeast Texas and southeast Oklahoma, and Paris Junior College has been here since 1924. Farming, rail and manufacturing have all shaped the job base, and employers change over time, so describe what is near your house today rather than relying on old lists.

Shoppers often want to know the distance to the college, a medical office or a rail line, so state those distances in your description. Population passed 25,898 by 2000, and demand tends to come from local families, landlords and people who work at the medical center.

This choice is time against dollars. Selling to a buyer with a mortgage may bring a higher price, yet you pay an agent, host showings, answer inspection requests and wait on the lender. A cash buyer removes most of that hassle. The price is lower, but the closing date is yours and the repair money stays with you.

If the roof is worn, the wiring is dated or the foundation is in question, a cash sale can net about the same once repairs and commissions are taken out. A tidy house in a sought-after spot may do better listed. Obtain a written cash offer and a realistic listing estimate, then see which leaves more with you.

Find out who pays for the title policy, how many days closing will take, and whether the price can change after a walkthrough. Request proof of funds, and learn how much earnest money goes down and when it comes back.

Walk away from anyone who wants a fee before making an offer or refuses to write terms down. A solid offer spells out price, closing date, cost split and what happens to the deposit if the sale collapses.

In a smaller market like Paris, it is fair to ask how many local houses the buyer has closed and whether this title company has worked with them before.

A tenant with a lease changes who can show the house and when it can close. Gather the signed lease and deposit record, and tell each buyer up front whether the tenant plans to stay. Some investors want the lease and the rent income to continue, while others need a vacant house at closing.

Do not promise a move-out date you cannot control. If you need the tenant gone before the sale, start that process early and ask an attorney about the steps, because the timeline is fixed by the court, not by the buyer.

After you accept, the title company starts a file, orders the tax certificate and searches the Lamar County clerk's records for liens. When a lender is owed, they request that payoff on your behalf.

Bring photo ID on closing day and read the settlement statement, which lists the price, payoffs, prorated taxes and fees. When the deed is recorded, you are paid the balance. With no lender appraisal involved, the title search and your calendar mostly set the pace.

A surprise charge deserves an explanation before your signature, not after.

faqs.q: Is a cash sale faster than listing in Paris?
faqs.a: Usually, since nobody orders a lender appraisal and repair demands are rare. Your calendar and the title search decide the date. Listing may net more for a seller who can wait.

faqs.q: Which office answers questions about my Paris tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Lamar Central Appraisal District at (903) 785-7822. It covers values and exemptions and can name the office that collects your bill.

faqs.q: What is the Lamar protest deadline?
faqs.a: May 31 or 30 days from mailing of the notice, whichever comes later. Your notice prints the date that applies.

faqs.q: Is an inherited Paris house easy to sell?
faqs.a: Once ownership is on paper it is straightforward. That paper may be a probated will, a small estate affidavit or an affidavit of heirship, filed with the Lamar County clerk.

faqs.q: Do old fires or storms affect a sale?
faqs.a: They can steer what buyers ask. Hold onto repair receipts and state any known damage in plain words.
